articles.title_en: Russian publisher cuts Pushkin’s drinking stanza from third-grade textbook, citing anti-alcohol law. The Education Ministry’s response? Don’t do that — it’s Pushkin.
articles.lead_en: The news outlet Fontanka reported that a third-grade textbook, “Literaturnoye chteniye” (“Literary Reading”), published by Prosveshcheniye in 2023, includes an abridged version of Alexander Pushkin’s poem “Zimny vecher” (“Winter Evening”), known for its opening line, “The storm shrouds the sky in darkness.” The stanza in which the speaker suggests that his nanny join him in drinking “to drown our sorrows” was cut. The omission prompted a wave of mockery and outrage online, forcing the publisher to explain itself and the authorities to distance themselves from a textbook they themselves had approved.
